regimes.A: prediction already unique; family/explanation claim remains ambiguous
regimes.B: target claim and explanation remain ambiguous
regimes.C: claim already identified; correct action is stop/abstain
regimes.N: gauge-equivalent models have identical admissible sensor signatures; no intervention can identify ontology

intervention_class.type: continuous binary affine hyperplanes over current sensor signatures
intervention_class.action_equivalence: all distinct linearly separable bipartitions of the finite current fiber
intervention_class.feasibility: strict separability verified by linear programming

din_definition: after each observed response, the compatible model fiber is recomputed and Phi geometry is regenerated before synthesizing the next intervention
matched_no_reentry: the same initial Phi eigendirections and thresholds are optimized as a fixed open-loop batch and never recomputed after responses
primary_analysis: entire horizon curve H=1..4; no single horizon is the sole preregistered endpoint
endpoints: matched TOS reentry vs no-reentry difference
policy regret versus exact dynamic programming
correct abstention in C and N

support_interpretation.din_reentry_local_support: requires improvement over matched no-reentry on the horizon curve without false promotion
support_interpretation.nonreducibility: requires superiority over exact dynamic programming; equivalence or inferiority blocks the claim

hard_limits: finite generated model fibers are explicitly available to exact baselines
continuous interventions collapse to finitely many response partitions on each finite fiber
this is a policy/DIN test, not an external physical-world validation
